newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: CRICKET-LARA OUT FIRST BALL AS WEST INDIES SLUMP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LARA OUT FIRST BALL AS WEST INDIES SLUMP.

text.p: West Indies failed to recover from the first-ball dismissal of Brian Lara and were routed for 121 by India in the second one-day international on Sunday.
Put in to bat, West Indies lost opener Stuart Williams (3) and Lara (0) to consecutive balls from Venkatesh Prasad, who bowled impressively with fellow paceman Abey Kuruvilla.
West Indies were 14 for two after six overs when rain caused the first of two interruptions at Queen's Park Oval.
After play resumed, Kuruvilla accounted for Carl Hooper (14), Shivnarine Chanderpaul (12) and Roland Holder (0), the last two falling to brilliant catches by wicketkeeper Syed Karim.

Off-spinner Noel David chipped in with three wickets and despite a half-century stand between Jimmy Adams, who ran out of partners in making 35, and Ian Bishop (31), West Indies slumped to their lowest one-day total against India.
West Indies won the opening game here on Saturday but India have 46 overs to reach the modest target and square the four-match series.
